ai_show_review.summary: Blues‑heavy early set with standout Viola Lee Blues and Pigpen vocals
ai_show_review.blurb: The March 12 1966 Danish Center set delivers a tight blues‑driven performance highlighted by Next Time You See Me, In The Midnight Hour and Pigpen’s lead on Beat It On Down The Line. Jerry supplies surprising lead licks while the band keeps the energy high throughout. Soundboard sources capture the raw feel with generally good audio despite some background hiss.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at the Danish Center on March 12, 1966 is a pure early‑Dead blues romp that still feels fresh after all these years. The first set rolls from acoustic folk numbers into electrified blues, landing on a scorching Viola Lee Blues where Jerry’s lead licks cut through with an almost horn‑like bite and Pigpen drives the vocal charge on Beat It On Down The Line. Throughout the night the band maintains a high‑energy groove; Next Time You See Me showcases Phil’s steady, if slightly choppier, bass foundation while Bob (Pigpen) adds his trademark organ growl and gritty harmonica. Though the recordings vary—some soundboard tapes suffer minor hiss and an audience tape pushes Jerry’s guitar forward—the overall picture is a cohesive, soulful set that captures the Dead in their formative, blues‑obsessed prime.

best_recording.reason: Historically rich soundboard capture with generally good audio and tight blues‑heavy mix, despite minor hiss.

key_highlights: Tight blues‑heavy set that flows from acoustic roots into electrified jams.
Stellar Viola Lee Blues performance with soaring guitar and powerful Pigpen vocals.
High‑energy renditions of Next Time You See Me, In The Midnight Hour and Beat It On Down The Line.
Good soundboard recording captures the raw feel; minor hiss does not detract from overall enjoyment.

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers surprising lead licks, a horn‑like solo on In The Midnight Hour and strong vocal moments, keeping the band’s energy blazing.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a solid bass groove; though slightly choppier than later years, his lines lock in with the drums and drive the jams.
band_performance.Bob: Pigpen’s vocals dominate Beat It On Down The Line and other blues numbers; his organ and harmonica add gritty texture throughout.
band_performance.Ron \"Pigpen\" McKernan: Commands the keyboards, harmonica and vocal front‑line, delivering the soulful backbone of the set.
band_performance.Billy: Drums are present but often thin in the mix; on some recordings they disappear when volume is lowered, yet his rhythmic pulse underpins the high‑energy flow.
